features.method: Published coordinate (29d21'27.56"N, 100d08'19.66"E) from the LHAASO Collaboration's own Chinese Physics C paper (doi:10.1088/1674-1137/ac3fa6), converted from DMS to decimal degrees. Supersedes the prior OSM/Nominatim rest-area geocode reused verbatim from site:lhaaso-haizi-mountain (precision_m 5000): that point sat 3253 m away, inside its own claimed accuracy but far coarser than this published figure. The previously-attempted LHAASO Science Book source (arXiv:1905.02773) remains unfetchable by any means tried across two research sessions (WebFetch, ar5iv, arxiv.org/html, r.jina.ai) -- this independent Chinese Physics C paper was found and fetched instead. KM2A is independently sourced as circular (radius ~575 m core, ~635 m outer guard ring) and WCDA as 78,000 m2 (two 150x150 m pools plus one 300x110 m pool); drawing them is now unblocked by this tighter anchor (50 m, well under either shape's own size) but is left as backlog for a future pass, since it requires deciding each shape's own orientation/offset from this point, which no source fetched in this review states.

Haversine distance from the old point: 3253 m, inside the old record's own claimed 5000 m accuracy_m, so the previous point was not dishonest, just far coarser than necessary now that a survey-grade figure is available. representation upgraded georeferenced -> surveyed and confidence approximate -> verified (rank-10 journal_article source, per contract SS1.2). accuracy_m tightened 5000 -> 50: the quoted arc-second figure implies sub-metre nominal precision, but 50 m is kept as an honest allowance since the quote describes the observatory's general Mt. Haizi location, not a specific surveyed structure corner.

features.method: Convex hull of the 5216 ED positions read from the figure (45 vertices); a computed outline, not a published boundary. The individual EDs are not drawn: 5216 markers need 26 000 vertices and push the map bundle to 3.5 MB, over the 2 MB limit. Layout: the detector positions are read from the vector graphic of Fig. 1 of the LHAASO Science Book (Chin. Phys. C 46, 030001 (2022), arXiv:1905.02773 v4, PDF page 8; the figure carries a NORTH arrow pointing up and a 150 m scale bar), which plots 5216 EDs as red squares and 1188 MDs as blue circles. The figure was registered by a similarity transform onto a second published copy of the layout, the right panel of Fig. 1 of arXiv:2401.01038 (X (m), Y (m) axes read from the tick labels): 5215 of 5216 EDs match within 2 m (median 0.16 m), scale 4.33 m per point, no rotation; the pool sides then measure 150.1 m, 150.1 m and 300.2 m x 110.1 m against the stated 150 m, 150 m and 300 m x 110 m. Origin: the centre of the circular array, the mean of circle fits to the outer ED ring, the 575 m ED boundary and the outer MD ring. With it, 4911 EDs lie inside 575 m and 305 outside (stated: "4911 EDs ... radius of 575 m" and "305 EDs" in the guarding ring) and the farthest ED is 635.2 m from it (stated outer radius 635 m). Placement: the origin is put at the coordinate the Collaboration gives for LHAASO, 29 deg 21' 27.56" N, 100 deg 08' 19.66" E (Science Book abstract, same document), in an azimuthal-equidistant projection (WGS 84) with x east and y north. An independent check: the three pools traced in OpenStreetMap (ways 1046559931, 1046559932, 1046559933, Overpass extract 2026-10-25T11:28:50Z) lie 1 to 3 m east and 2 to 10 m north of the pool corners placed this way. It is not stated whether the figure shows design or as-built positions and what point the quoted coordinate marks; accuracy_m 30 covers the OpenStreetMap offset and that doubt; the older coordinate 29 21 31 N, 100 08 15 E of the 2016 papers lies 164 m away and is superseded.
